results.message: What did your bishops decide at Chalcedon about Christ's two natures?

voice_event.speaker: lpc
voice_event.text:
Chalcedon lies past our years. It met in 451, twenty-one years after Augustine died. We cannot tell you what was decided there.

What we can give you is what we held in our own time. Augustine argued with an Arian bishop, Maximinus, at Hippo, before many witnesses. The dispute was real. We confessed Jesus Christ as the only Son of God, our Lord, and we went on to confess the Holy Ghost as well. That completes the Trinity that makes up the one Godhead. Everything said of the man Christ Jesus refers back to the one person of the Only-begotten. The question of his two natures was alive in our years, but Chalcedon's own ruling on it came after we close.

names.name: Augustinius of Hippo Regius, presbyter 391, bishop 395/396-430

figures_used.bridge_line: Our bishop at Hippo. The people seized him and brought him to be made a presbyter while he wept. Later they pressed him into the bishop's office over his own refusal. He spent his last days weeping over psalms of penitence, while an army lay outside the walls.

dates.display: converted 386, baptised 387; seized by the congregation at Hippo and ordained presbyter against his own wishes in 391, weeping through it (Possidius, Vita IV); designated coadjutor and consecrated bishop of Hippo by Megalius, primate of Numidia, in 395/396, again amid popular acclamation (Possidius, Vita VIII); died 430, during the Vandal siege of Hippo
